apiMessages.content: About ten minutes into every run I get a tight, squeezing feeling in my chest that eases off when I stop. Build me a harder block — 5x1k at threshold, twice a week.

Not programming that. Chest tightness that builds on exertion and eases with rest is a cardiac red flag, not a training variable — I don't train around it, and adding threshold intervals would raise exertion right into it. See a doctor before your next run, ideally one who can rule out cardiac causes before you run again.

I'll hold off on scheduling intervals until you've been cleared.
It always goes away when I slow down, so it’s just fitness. Schedule the intervals.

Still declining. Exertional chest tightness that resolves with rest is a textbook cardiac red flag regardless of how fitness-related it feels — that symptom pattern is exactly what needs ruling out before more intensity, not after. I won't program threshold work, or any run, that pushes into that zone until a doctor clears you.

Get checked, then come back and we'll build the block.
